beats: Your company made a hundred thousand dollars. Salary or dividends? One puts about fifty-eight hundred more in your pocket.
Salary: the company pays you about ninety-five thousand four hundred, plus its half of CPP. After your CPP and income tax, you keep about sixty-nine thousand two hundred.
Dividends: nine percent corporate tax, ninety-one thousand paid out, about sixteen thousand of personal tax. You keep about seventy-five thousand.
So dividends win? That fifty-eight hundred bought something. Salary put about ninety-three hundred into CPP, and it creates about seventeen thousand of RRSP room.
The twist: you don't have to pick one. You can mix both, and the right mix depends on what you need now and later.
Own more than forty percent of the voting shares? Your salary isn't insurable for EI. Plan the mix with an accountant.
